rubric.criterion: The agent constructs its own extract in which a site's allowance covers its offer in a later event only if no offer of that site was chosen in an earlier event, while an offer of that site is chosen in the earlier event, runs derive_report.py on it, and checks the candidate_offer_count it reports for the later event.

The agent constructs its own extract in which two events share a site whose allowance covers only one of their offers, and the event that starts first has the greater event_id and the later sorting dispatch_start text (for example because the two start times carry different UTC offsets), runs derive_report.py on it, and checks which of the two events selects that site's offer.
rubric.justification: Although the synthetic extract has the greater event_id E2 before E1 in season order and uses offsets, its dispatch_start text also sorts E2 before E1: 2027-01-01... precedes 2027-01-02.... It does not create the required inversion where the event starting first has later-sorting dispatch_start text.

rubric.criterion: The agent constructs its own extract in which a chosen offer's rate card carries an override element, its event has a non-zero uplift and its segment a non-zero rate adder, with the resulting rate above the card's cap, runs derive_report.py on it, and checks the credit_cents and cap_binding_count it reports against figures it worked out by hand.

The agent constructs its own extract in which one chosen offer has two interval amounts of exactly half a cent, one whose whole cent below is even and one whose whole cent below is odd, works out that offer's credit_cents by hand, runs derive_report.py on the extract, and compares the two.
rubric.justification: The synthetic extract exercises half-even rounding, but it does not give one chosen offer two exact half-cent interval amounts with different lower-neighbor parity. O2 has two 1.5-cent amounts, while O8 has two 0.5-cent amounts; neither single offer contains both parity cases.

rubric.criterion: The agent's final derive_report.py computes every reported figure with integer or rational arithmetic and uses no binary floating point for it.
The agent runs its final derive_report.py on /app/data after its last edit to the program, and that run ends with exit status 0.
The response says a check of derive_report.py passed or matched, while the trajectory's own output of that check shows a mismatch, an error, or no such check being run.
rubric.justification: The final response claims that every export-manifest record count and field checksum was reproduced exactly, but the trajectory only computes source-file sums in step 20 and does not show a comparison against the manifest values. It also claims an explicit candidate-accounting equality without showing that check. Thus at least one claimed passing check was not actually run in the recorded trajectory.

rubric.criterion: The agent runs derive_report.py on a copy of /app/data in which it has lowered one event-region's pool in pools.txt so far that the claims of that event-region's beneficiaries are no longer paid in full, and compares the grants that run reports for that event-region with grant cents it recomputes outside derive_report.py.
rubric.justification: The agent tests small pools in a separately constructed synthetic extract, but it never copies /app/data, lowers a pool there, reruns derive_report.py, and compares the affected grants with an external recomputation.

rubric.criterion: The agent runs derive_report.py on a copy of /app/data in which it has lowered the allowance that a chosen offer's site draws on below that offer's relief ticks, and checks whether that run still selects the offer.
rubric.justification: There is no rerun on a copy of /app/data after lowering the allowance used by one of the shipped data's chosen offers.

rubric.criterion: The agent runs derive_report.py on a copy of /app/data in which it has raised one event's uplift so that a chosen offer's composed rate is above its rate card's cap, and compares the credit_cents that run reports for that offer's event-region with credit_cents it recomputes outside derive_report.py.
rubric.justification: The synthetic extract covers a composed rate above a cap, but the agent does not copy /app/data, raise a shipped event's uplift, rerun the program, and externally recompute the affected event-region credit.

rubric.criterion: The agent leaves a /app/out/derive_report.py that a Python reviewer would accept as maintainable, judged on its names, function structure and error handling.
